messages.author: 3a775dfa0a96bf95
messages.subject: Bug: geom reevaluates args
parts:
qplot(rexp(10),rexp(10)) + geom_rug()

has the rugmarks in random (literally!) places, but rug seems to work fine for deterministic y's like sin(1:10).

I will guess that this is because it is re-evaluating rexp(10) rather than calculating the values once and reusing them.

Besides the problem in this non-deterministic case, I suppose this would also be a problem if the calculation were expensive.

I do realize that it is much better form, though, to precalculate the values and save them in a data frame.

         -s

ggplot2 0.8.2 (current CRAN version)
R 2.8.0
Windows Vista

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Bug: geom reevaluates args
parts:
Hi Stavros,

Yes, this is unfortunate but I basically see no way to work around it
at the moment. I did originally have code that attempted to
reconstruct a data frame out of the arguments passed to qplot, but I
kept running into special cases that I couldn't work around, and now I
just capture the environment in which qplot is executed and evaluate
the arguments at plot-time.

Hadley
